# Tintpad: Free macOS Launcher for Claude Code, Codex & Coding Agents

> Tintpad is a free, open source (MIT) macOS menu-bar launcher for coding agents. Press a hotkey and a black drop falls out of the Mac's notch with your repos inside. Return opens your own terminal at that repo with Claude Code, Codex, or any coding agent already running. Native Swift/SwiftUI, signed and notarized, local-only, no accounts, no telemetry. Built by Erik Nielsen (sorkila.com).

## What is Tintpad?

Tintpad is a launcher for the agent loop: repo → terminal → coding agent. Instead of cd-ing around and retyping agent commands, you press a global hotkey, a black capsule (the drop) falls from the notch showing your repos ranked by frecency, you pick one, and Return opens your real terminal at that repo with your chosen agent already running. Macs without a notch get the same drop as a floating pill below the menu bar.

Tintpad hands off to your terminal, it isn't one. It is not a terminal replacement, not a Raycast extension, and not a shell wrapper you live inside.

## App Details

- **Platform:** macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later. Native Swift/SwiftUI, menu-bar app.
- **Price:** Free. The whole app, no functional gates. Optional pay-what-you-want Supporter tip unlocks a cosmetic tinted-chip perk.
- **License:** MIT, fully open source: https://github.com/sorkila/tintpad
- **Distribution:** Signed and notarized by Apple.
- **Privacy:** Local-only. Your repo list is a JSON file on your Mac. No accounts, no telemetry, nothing leaves your machine.
- **Developer:** Erik Nielsen (solo indie developer, Sweden): https://sorkila.com
- **Website:** https://tintpad.com

## Install

Two ways, both free:

- **Homebrew:** `brew install --cask sorkila/tap/tintpad`
- **Direct download (DMG):** https://github.com/sorkila/tintpad/releases/latest/download/Tintpad.dmg

Auto-updates via Sparkle after install.

## Supported Terminals (7)

Ghostty, iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm, Alacritty, Terminal.app, Warp. Tintpad opens the chosen terminal at the repo with the command already running. Only Ghostty needs the macOS Accessibility permission (there is no other way to hand it a command); the others need Automation or nothing.

## Key Differentiators

- **Agent-native:** built around launching Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agent CLIs, not generic app launching. Each repo remembers the agent and run mode it last used.
- **Run-mode safety:** two chips always state exactly what Return will run (the agent and the mode). The mode that skips permissions is shown in red and asks for confirmation twice.
- **Frecency ranking:** your most-used repos float to the top. ⌘0 replays the last session.
- **Worktrees:** one keystroke creates an isolated git branch checkout with the agent launched in it.
- **Hands off to YOUR terminal:** unlike Raycast (which runs things inside Raycast), Tintpad opens your real terminal.
- **No config:** works out of the box, imports repos from GitHub or a folder scan.
- **Free and inspectable:** MIT license, the entire source is on GitHub.
